I have been working this land in Quzhou for 45 years. I know every corner of my 13.1 mu. My sons have gone to work in the city, so it is mainly me managing the farm now, though I can hire machines for the heavy work. My plan is the same as always — wheat in winter, maize in summer, on all my land.

**Wheat:** I plant in October like I always do. I will buy Jimai seeds from the township supply station — I have used this variety for many years and I trust it. At planting I spread compound fertilizer into the soil, then I topdress urea at jointing stage. I irrigate three times: once when I sow to help germination, once at jointing, once at heading if the weather is dry. I spray herbicide in early spring and then again for aphids and mildew before heading. My neighbor uses no-tillage but I still like to rotary till before wheat — the soil feels right when I do it that way.

**Maize:** After wheat harvest in June I go straight into maize. I buy Zhengdan 958 — I have planted this hybrid for more than 15 years, it does not let me down. The ground is still loose from wheat so I direct seed without deep tilling. I fertilize at planting with compound fertilizer, then topdress urea at big bell stage. Two irrigations if the summer is dry. One spray for corn borer or armyworm if I see them. My son comes home in autumn to help me hire the combine for harvest.

I do not change what works. At 68 I know what this land needs.
